correctness.rationale: P1–P4 force the top row, absorption by intersection with the antecedent, and monotonicity. P5 after absorption is exactly the displayed constraint for d ⊆ a; self-coherence rules out a doubleton's other atom in a singleton column unless the value is top. Thus all constraints between distinct nontrivial rows run from singleton rows to doubleton rows. P5 at c=0 and consequent monotonicity give antitonicity of N, and double-negation inflation plus antitonicity is equivalent to self-adjointness. Testing against singletons then yields the common-neighbor polarity of a loop-free undirected graph. The smaller carriers have forced top and bottom rows (including the single-element carrier if allowed); on the two-atom carrier only singleton rows remain. Independent replay: `python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 2` enumerated 512000 candidate full tables at three atoms after P1–P4, identity and semicomplementation, applied P5 to complete tables, and obtained 7820 T and 1021 F. It matched all sixteen orbit-size and projected-row triples and F fibers 729, 81, 16, 1 with multiplicities 1, 3, 3, 1; the smaller carriers give (T,F)=(1,1),(1,1),(4,2) for zero to two atoms with distinct negations in each class. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.
